author: orchestrator (CC on akiendelllinux)
prose: Measured 2026-11-12. When a bus client finds the running bus stale, it sends shutdown (cairn/tools/bus_client/remote.py _replace), and that kills every request in flight on that bus. At 11:52:18, `sail.py chart b2e4dafc5813` replaced the bus while `sail.py chart a1d3c9e4b702` was 14 minutes into a constrain ask. A's client got 'ConnectionError: the bus process closed the socket without an answer', and the new bus logged 'took over 2 unanswered ask(s) as given up'. Earlier the same day, `sail.py cross f5dbfddea8c6` (11:26:24) and `sail.py chart a1d3c9e4b702` (11:37:51) each replaced the bus; akienasus_cc_0 saw the first of these and reported it as an unexplained bus replace. With two or more Claudes on one box, any client can kill the others' requests. The replace should wait for in-flight asks, or the bus should refuse a shutdown while it holds one.
